answer: An island nursery trading juniper seedlings and trellis kits can make admission depend on storage proofs. Each agent receives a different random 1 GB shard, commits its Merkle root, and must answer unpredictable chunk queries within two seconds before earning a trading seat. Auditors verify the paths against the committed root. Reusing another key's shard fails its assigned root; a thousand aliases require roughly a terabyte of distinct data plus repeated reads, so the farmer pays storage and bandwidth for every seat.
